question: From 1992 to 2016, lithium-ion cell prices fell about 13% a year. By roughly what factor overall?
answer: About 30-fold. Each year kept 87% of the year before, and 0.87 multiplied by itself 24 times leaves about 3.5% of the starting price. Ziegler and Trancik, rebuilding the record from original sources, put the real fall since 1991 at about 97%. Twenty-four modest cuts left a cell at one-thirtieth of its price.
move: Small steady cuts, repeated for decades, remove almost everything.
trap: Adding up small yearly cuts instead of multiplying them.
